# Corrected PromptForge Walkthrough Video Brief

## Correction approach

The first video versions used viewport-only screen frames, which did not reveal complete pages or enough of the relevant controls. The revised landscape and mobile videos use **full-page captures with slow top-to-bottom screen movement**. Each voice-over scene describes only controls visible during that scene. The revised videos are intentionally longer and have no rapid cuts.

## Narration and visual alignment

| Scene | Visible page and movement | Voice-over script |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Builder: header and category cards | “Welcome to PromptForge. This is the Builder, your starting point for turning an idea into a useful AI brief. Use these category cards to choose the kind of work you want to make.” |
| 2 | Builder: guided fields and live output | “After choosing a category, describe what you are making, your primary goal, audience, platform, tone, and any helpful details. The live prompt updates as you decide.” |
| 3 | Builder: output actions | “Review the live prompt before you use it. Copy sends it to your clipboard. Save keeps work on your account after sign-in. Refine lets you adjust the brief.” |
| 4 | Library: heading and search | “Open Library from the header to start with a proven prompt. Search by a keyword, then narrow the results with the category and access filters.” |
| 5 | Library: catalog cards and pagination | “Browse the prompt cards at your own pace. Use sorting and Load more to move through the catalog, then open a prompt to adapt its structure.” |
| 6 | Pricing: plans and unlock path | “On Pricing, compare the free shelf with full access. You can keep using free prompts, or follow the unlock path when you need the complete workshop.” |
| 7 | Sign in: account benefits and choices | “Sign in with your email, magic link, Google, or GitHub when available. Signing in keeps saved prompts and your access details connected to your account.” |
| 8 | Guides: article and navigation | “Visit the Guides for practical prompt-engineering examples. Each guide explains a method, then links you back to the Builder or Library to put it into practice.” |
| 9 | About: mission and audience | “About explains the PromptForge mission and who it is built for: creators, marketers, freelancers, developers, and teams who need clearer AI instructions.” |
| 10 | Contact and theme controls | “Use Contact to send a message or open WhatsApp. You can also choose dark, light, or system appearance from the theme control, and navigate easily from the mobile menu.” |
| 11 | Builder: closing summary | “That is the PromptForge workflow: build a brief, browse templates, learn the method, and get help when you need it.” |

## Pacing standard

Each scene should stay on screen through its full matching narration, plus two seconds of reading time. The page motion must remain slow enough to see all major visible sections and controls.

# Corrected Walkthrough Video Review

The revised desktop walkthrough was checked at the Library search-and-filter scene. The full-width heading, search bar, category selector, access filters, sorting control, and first catalog cards remain clearly visible while the matching Library narration plays.

The revised mobile walkthrough was checked at the Contact scene. The slow vertical movement shows the direct email, phone, WhatsApp, contact form, and the Chat on WhatsApp action at readable scale. This aligns with the matching narration about sending a message or opening WhatsApp.

Both corrected outputs contain voice-over audio and run for approximately 194 seconds. The desktop output is 1280×720 and the mobile output is 1080×1920.

# Paid-Domain DNS Incident Notes

On 2026-08-26, a mobile Chrome screenshot reported `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` for `www.promptforge.com.ng`.

At investigation time, independent Cloudflare and Google DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers both returned successful A-record answers for the apex and `www` hostnames. The domain delegation resolves to `ns1.vercel-dns.com` and `ns2.vercel-dns.com`. The linked Vercel project includes both `promptforge.com.ng` and `www.promptforge.com.ng`; its latest production deployment is Ready.

HTTPS verification returned `200` from Vercel for `https://www.promptforge.com.ng/` and a `308` redirect from the apex to the `www` hostname. This establishes that the observed phone error was not present on independent public DNS checks at investigation time. The next diagnostic step is a cached-resolver/device retest rather than modifying an already resolving domain record.

# PromptForge Mobile Walkthrough Video Brief

## Format and pacing

This is a **9:16 portrait mobile walkthrough** for new users. It uses a deliberately paced screen tour: each major scene remains visible for **at least eight seconds** so viewers can read the page, find the key controls, and understand the next step. Captions appear in a persistent lower-third and stay on screen for the complete scene.

## Scene sequence

| Scene | Page | Minimum dwell time | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Builder | 9 seconds | Start from the Builder and choose a category. |
| 2 | Builder | 9 seconds | Complete the guided brief and watch the live output take shape. |
| 3 | Library | 9 seconds | Search the prompt shelf, use filters, and browse prompt work orders. |
| 4 | Pricing | 8 seconds | Explain free access and the optional lifetime unlock path. |
| 5 | Sign in | 8 seconds | Explain email sign-in, magic-link access, and saved work. |
| 6 | Guides | 8 seconds | Show learning resources for clearer prompts and better workflows. |
| 7 | About | 8 seconds | Show the mission and who PromptForge is built for. |
| 8 | Contact | 9 seconds | Show the contact form and direct WhatsApp route. |
| 9 | Builder | 9 seconds | Close with the header navigation and the next prompt-building step. |

## Accuracy constraints

Use real mobile screens and visible controls only. Do not show personal account data, redemption codes, admin settings, a purchase completion, or invented user feedback.

# PromptForge 30-Second Mobile Social Teaser

This teaser is **1080×1920 (9:16)** and 30 seconds long. It begins with an animated text-only **PROMPTFORGE** wordmark: `PROMPT` appears in white, then `FORGE` resolves in ember orange with a brief glowing underline. The opening must stay clear for three seconds before the product demonstration begins.

The Builder, Library, and Contact scenes use responsive PromptForge screens and match the corresponding narration about categories and live output, searching the prompt library, and contacting support through WhatsApp or the form.

# PromptForge Uptime Monitoring

## Active monitor

PromptForge is monitored externally at **https://www.promptforge.com.ng/** using UptimeRobot’s no-dashboard quick-monitor workflow. The monitor was activated by the owner through the activation email sent to **saintpaulek@gmail.com**.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Monitored URL | `https://www.promptforge.com.ng/` |
| Check type | External HTTPS availability check |
| Check frequency | Every 5 minutes |
| Alert recipient | `saintpaulek@gmail.com` |
| Alert events | Downtime and recovery |
| Ownership | PromptForge owner |

The current health check returned HTTP `200` for the homepage. The public Library endpoint also returned HTTP `200` with JSON, so the catalog is available at the time of verification.

## When an alert arrives

First open `https://www.promptforge.com.ng/` using both mobile data and Wi-Fi. If the browser reports a DNS issue, review **Vercel → PromptForge → Settings → Domains** and confirm that both `promptforge.com.ng` and `www.promptforge.com.ng` show **Valid Configuration**. If the homepage works but Library does not, test `https://www.promptforge.com.ng/library` and the catalog route before changing any DNS records.

> Do not remove domain records while the site is reachable. Verify the alert from a second network first, because temporary local-network problems can mimic an outage.

If the issue persists across networks, retain the downtime email and contact the site maintainer with the time of the alert, the affected URL, and any browser error text. The recovery alert indicates that the monitor can reach the homepage again.

# PromptForge Product Walkthrough Video Brief

## Format and purpose

This walkthrough is a polished **16:9 landscape product tutorial** for new PromptForge users. It uses the live Workshop Noir visual language and explains the public product journey in plain English. The video must demonstrate real pages and workflows rather than inventing unavailable features.

## Storyboard

| Segment | Page or action | On-screen guidance |
|---|---|---|
| Opening | Builder homepage | Introduce PromptForge and the Builder as the starting point. |
| Build a prompt | Builder | Choose a category, answer the guided brief, inspect the live output, then copy or refine it. |
| Find a template | Library | Use search, category filters, access filters, sorting, and Load more work orders. |
| Access | Pricing and account context | Explain free prompts, locked work orders, signing in, and unlocking full access without exposing codes or credentials. |
| Learn | Guides and About | Show practical guides, the editorial profile, and PromptForge’s mission. |
| Get help | Contact | Show the contact form and direct WhatsApp contact path. |
| Personalize | Header theme control | Demonstrate dark, light, and system theme choices plus responsive navigation. |
| Closing | Builder and Library | Reinforce the build, browse, learn, and contact path. |

## Accuracy constraints

The video should not depict an authenticated account, code redemption, admin controls, a completed purchase, personal information, or any fabricated testimonials. It should use the exact text-only **PROMPTFORGE** branding and dark industrial orange-and-charcoal Workshop Noir palette.

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

ROOT = Path('/home/ubuntu/promptforge')
FRAMES = ROOT / 'portrait_frames'
SEGMENTS = ROOT / 'portrait_segments'
SEGMENTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
scenes = [
    ('intro.png', 6),
    ('choose.png', 8),
    ('builder_mobile.png', 10),
    ('details.png', 10),
    ('preview.png', 10),
    ('library_card.png', 7),
    ('library_mobile.png', 10),
    ('account.png', 8),
    ('unlock.png', 8),
    ('outro.png', 7),
]
for index, (filename, duration) in enumerate(scenes, 1):
    source = FRAMES / filename
    output = SEGMENTS / f'{index:02d}.mp4'
    fade_out = max(0, duration - 0.35)
    vf = (
        f"scale=720:1280:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,"
        f"crop=720:1280,format=yuv420p,"
        f"fade=t=in:st=0:d=0.35,fade=t=out:st={fade_out}:d=0.35"
    )
    subprocess.run([
        'ffmpeg', '-y', '-loglevel', 'error', '-loop', '1', '-i', str(source),
        '-t', str(duration), '-vf', vf, '-r', '25', '-an', '-pix_fmt', 'yuv420p', str(output)
    ], check=True)
concat_file = ROOT / 'portrait_concat.txt'
concat_file.write_text('\n'.join(f"file '{(SEGMENTS / f'{i:02d}.mp4').as_posix()}'" for i in range(1, len(scenes) + 1)) + '\n')
video_only = ROOT / 'portrait_video_only.mp4'
subprocess.run([
    'ffmpeg', '-y', '-loglevel', 'error', '-f', 'concat', '-safe', '0', '-i', str(concat_file),
    '-c', 'copy', str(video_only)
], check=True)
final = ROOT / 'promptforge_new_user_walkthrough_9x16.mp4'
subprocess.run([
    'ffmpeg', '-y', '-loglevel', 'error', '-i', str(video_only), '-i', str(ROOT / 'walkthrough_narration_final.wav'),
    '-map', '0:v:0', '-map', '1:a:0', '-c:v', 'copy', '-c:a', 'aac', '-b:a', '128k',
    '-shortest', '-movflags', '+faststart', str(final)
], check=True)
print(final)

# PromptForge backlink outreach foundation

PromptForge should earn external links from relevant places where the product is genuinely useful. The first targets should be the founder’s verified professional profiles, the company’s Google Business Profile if eligible, Nigerian technology and startup directories, creator and marketing communities that allow useful resource links, and guest contributions to publications focused on AI productivity, content operations, freelancing, and customer engagement.

Each placement should point to the most relevant page rather than always linking to the homepage. A directory profile can link to `/about`; a practical tutorial can link to `/guides/prompt-engineering` if that route is later created; and a resource mention can link to `/library` or `/pricing` when the surrounding copy makes that destination useful. Use descriptive, natural anchor text such as “PromptForge’s structured AI prompt builder,” not repeated exact-match keywords.

## Outreach note

Subject: Practical resource for clearer AI briefs

Hello [Name],

I’m sharing PromptForge, a practical AI prompt builder and searchable prompt library for creators, marketers, freelancers, developers, and small teams. We published a short field guide on turning a rough idea into a useful AI brief. If it fits an upcoming article, resource page, or community discussion about AI productivity, you’re welcome to review it and link to it where it genuinely helps your readers.

Resource: https://www.promptforge.com.ng/about

Best,
Saint Paul Ekuerre
PromptForge

## Quality rules

Only request links from pages whose audience is relevant to PromptForge. Do not buy links, exchange links at scale, publish duplicate guest articles, or claim customer results that have not been documented. Keep a simple outreach log with the site, page, contact, date, requested destination, and outcome. Review links quarterly and ask for corrections when a placement becomes misleading or irrelevant.

# Google SEO guidance notes

Google Search Central states that Organization structured data on the homepage or a page describing the organization can help Google understand administrative details and disambiguate the organization. It recommends adding only properties that apply and validating the markup with the Rich Results Test.

Google also states that structured data should describe information visible on the page; it should not be added for content that is not visible. FAQ markup is therefore limited to the questions and answers visibly presented on PromptForge’s Contact page.

Google’s link guidance says crawlable links should use an anchor element with an href, descriptive anchor text, and natural context. It recommends cross-referencing important internal pages and obtaining external links naturally rather than using keyword-stuffed or paid/untrusted links.

# PromptForge Design Direction

## Three possible stylistic approaches

### Theme Name: Workshop Noir
Very Brief Intro: A dark, tactile digital workshop inspired by forged metal, ember light, and precision tools. It makes prompt-building feel like a craft rather than a form.
Probability: 0.07

### Theme Name: Editorial Signal
Very Brief Intro: A high-contrast magazine-like interface with oversized typography, clean paper-like surfaces, and orange editorial marks. It positions PromptForge as a confident creative utility.
Probability: 0.03

### Theme Name: Control Room
Very Brief Intro: A dark operator dashboard with technical readouts, warm orange status lights, and modular panels. It emphasizes speed, control, and repeatable output.
Probability: 0.06

## Chosen Approach: Workshop Noir

### Design Movement
Industrial editorialism: the visual language of a premium maker’s workshop translated into a focused SaaS tool.

### Core Principles
1. **Craft over clutter** — every control should feel purposeful, with strong hierarchy and generous breathing room.
2. **Warm precision** — pair near-black surfaces and steel-gray dividers with ember orange for action and progress.
3. **Visible making** — show the prompt forming in real time so the interface feels alive and instructive.
4. **Useful drama** — use texture, glows, and motion as restrained accents around the work, never as decoration for its own sake.

### Color Philosophy
The base is a charcoal-black workshop floor, giving the prompt preview authority and reducing visual noise. Ember orange is the signature brand color: it signals energy, transformation, and the moment raw input becomes useful output. Steel, ash, and parchment neutrals separate content without making the UI feel sterile.

### Layout Paradigm
A split workbench rather than a centered landing page: a narrow contextual rail for the build steps and category, a broad materials area for inputs, and a sticky prompt output panel that remains the visual destination. Marketing pages use offset editorial sections and asymmetric orange rules.

### Signature Elements
- Orange forge-line rules that trace progress between builder steps.
- Brushed-metal panel headers with compact uppercase labels.
- A prompt preview treated like a finished work order, with structured sections and copy-ready output.

### Interaction Philosophy
Interactions should feel like tools being handled: immediate, tactile, and legible. Selecting a category changes the materials tray; generating a prompt produces a short forge pulse and updates the work order; copy and save actions confirm quietly with a compact toast.

### Animation
Use 150–240ms ease-out transitions for controls, 180ms button press scale feedback, and a restrained 700ms prompt-forge reveal when output changes. Stagger builder sections by 40ms on first entry. Never animate keyboard-driven interactions. Respect reduced-motion preferences.

### Typography System
Use **Space Grotesk** for display headings and **DM Sans** for interface copy. Headings should be tight, slightly oversized, and sentence case; labels use 11px uppercase with letter spacing; prompt output uses a readable 14–16px mono treatment only for code-like fragments, not the entire interface.

### Brand Essence
PromptForge is the practical prompt workshop for creators, marketers, and freelancers who want production-ready AI instructions without learning prompt theory. Personality: **capable, warm, exacting**.

### Brand Voice
Headlines are direct and energetic. CTAs describe the result, not the mechanism. Microcopy teaches without talking down.

Example lines:
- “Turn a rough idea into a prompt you can ship.”
- “Choose your materials. We’ll shape the instruction.”

### Wordmark & Logo
Use the supplied PromptForge logo as the primary wordmark, preserving the orange/white lockup and tool-forge symbol. In compact contexts, use the symbol-only mark inside a small dark square with an orange edge.

### Signature Brand Color
**Ember Orange — #F36B21.** It is the unmistakable action color for PromptForge: warm enough to feel human, vivid enough to guide the eye against charcoal.

## Product scope for this build

The first delivery will focus on a convincing static prototype with working client-side interactions: Builder with category-aware material fields for image and video generation, live structured prompt generation, copy/reset/refine affordances, Library with search/filter and locked states, About, Contact, Auth, and an Unlock flow. Backend-dependent auth, payments, email delivery, and admin persistence will be represented with clear UI states until a full-stack upgrade and service credentials are connected.

## Style Decisions

- Every non-builder page uses at least one Workshop Noir signature cue: an ember rule, uppercase workshop label, or work-order frame.
- Library items are catalogued prompt work orders with stamped readiness/lock states and structured metadata.
- Contact and utility pages use dark workbench surfaces, practical instructional microcopy, and ember-only primary actions.

Sign in to the GitHub account that owns or can write to `saintpaulek/prompt4orge`. The account must be able to push commits and create branches. In GitHub, open the repository and confirm that **Settings → Collaborators and teams** gives your active account write or maintain permission.

Open `https://github.com/saintpaulek/prompt4orge` and record the current commit shown on the `main` branch. At the time of the migration assessment, the old source was at commit `7d257e7243beb4810b079922998d5d87e49fa776`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/saintpaulek/prompt4orge.git
cd prompt4orge
git checkout -b backup-before-manus-promptforge
git push origin backup-before-manus-promptforge
```

Confirm that the branch appears on GitHub. If you prefer a tag, create one as well:

```bash

git push origin old-vercel-before-manus-migration
```

The backup branch or tag is the rollback point. Do not delete it until the new Vercel deployment has been tested in production.

## Phase 3: Prepare the current PromptForge source

Use the current PromptForge project as the source of truth. It is located locally at `/home/ubuntu/promptforge` in the Manus workspace. Confirm that the current source builds before copying it:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm test
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm build
```

Do not copy any `.env` files, private keys, database dumps, or local build output into GitHub. The repository should contain source code and configuration only. Secrets must be entered in Vercel’s Environment Variables panel, not committed to the repository.

Replace the old repository contents using one of these methods.

### Recommended method: replace the repository from a clean working copy

Make a second clone of the repository for the migration and preserve its `.git` directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/saintpaulek/prompt4orge.git prompt4orge-migration
cd prompt4orge-migration
git checkout main
```

Copy the current PromptForge project into that clone while excluding Git metadata, dependencies, local secrets, and build output. On Linux, an example is:

```bash
  --exclude='dist/' \
  --exclude='.env' \
```

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm build
```

Commit the replacement to a migration branch first:

```bash

git add -A
git commit -m "Replace legacy app with current PromptForge build"
git push origin migrate-current-manus-promptforge
```

Review the branch on GitHub. Only after the diff looks correct should you merge it into `main`:

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git merge --no-ff migrate-current-manus-promptforge -m "Deploy current PromptForge build"
git push origin main
```

The Vercel project is configured to deploy from the GitHub repository’s production branch. A new commit on `main` should create a new production deployment, but confirm this in Vercel before considering the migration complete.

def crop_16_9(source, output):
    image = Image.open(source).convert('RGB')
    width, height = image.size
    target_height = round(width * 9 / 16)
    if target_height > height:
        target_width = round(height * 16 / 9)
        left = (width - target_width) // 2
        box = (left, 0, left + target_width, height)
    else:
        top = max(0, (height - target_height) // 2)
        box = (0, top, width, top + target_height)
    image.crop(box).save(output)

# PromptForge New-User Walkthrough Video Brief

## Purpose
Create a concise onboarding video for first-time PromptForge users. The video should explain the product journey clearly and make the Builder feel approachable for beginners.

## Audience
New creators, marketers, freelancers, developers, educators, and small-business users who want to create better AI prompts without studying prompt theory.

## Target format
A 60–75 second landscape product walkthrough in the Workshop Noir aesthetic: black and charcoal surfaces, ember-orange accents, steel-gray details, clean editorial typography, subtle workshop/forge atmosphere, and restrained motion.

## Storyboard

| Time | Scene | On-screen message | Voiceover intent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–7s | Brand intro with PromptForge mark and dark forge texture | “Forge prompts that ship.” | Welcome the user and frame PromptForge as a practical prompt workshop. |
| 7–20s | Builder overview with category cards | “1. Choose what you’re making” | Explain that beginners can pick a category such as Social Media, Writing, Marketing, Code, Image, Video, Business, or Customer Service. |
| 20–34s | Builder controls and live work order preview | “2. Add a few details” | Show project type, audience, platform/format, tone, and primary goal; emphasize that no prompt theory is required. |
| 34–46s | Live preview assembles role, task, audience, format, tone, goal, deliverables, and constraints | “3. Watch your prompt take shape” | Explain that the structured preview updates as choices change and stays populated for every category. |
| 46–58s | Action row: Copy, Save, Refine, Reset | “4. Use it immediately” | Show copying the prompt, refining it, resetting it, and signing in to save work. |
| 58–68s | Library search and filters | “Browse 3,000 ready-to-use prompts” | Explain the searchable catalog, category filters, and FREE/LOCKED access states. |
| 68–75s | Unlock/account CTA and closing brand frame | “Start building in PromptForge” | Invite the viewer to try Builder first, then create an account or explore lifetime access when ready. |

## Visual constraints
Use authentic-looking product UI compositions with large readable labels, no invented testimonials, no fake ratings, and no claims beyond the product’s actual functions. Keep transitions smooth and short, with ember-orange highlights guiding attention. Avoid tiny illegible interface text, busy backgrounds behind instructional copy, and generic SaaS blue/purple styling.

## Delivery
Preferred output: MP4, 16:9, suitable for a landing-page onboarding section or first-login welcome modal. Include captions or readable on-screen labels so the video remains understandable without audio.
